attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. The refrain he quotes belongs to VCs, but his rebuttal is his own.

semantics.note: 'I don't think it'll happen quickly enough' is a plain statement of belief, not graded probability, so it counts as a forecast. The proposition leaves out the observation that he sees no proof yet, but that is a separate clause. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Reading 'these companies' as OpenAI and Anthropic, and 'turn things around' as reaching sustainable viability, is an ordinary reading of the passage. Requiring lasting recovery or terminal failure before resolving is reasonable given there is no deadline.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own disclosure of benchmark throughput gains. It does not measure OpenAI's or Anthropic's costs or finances.

Anthropic S-1, available before the cutoff. It shows operating income and cash-flow gains alongside net losses. It does not separate out chip-driven savings, does not show lasting viability, and does not cover OpenAI.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline, and nothing meets the early-resolution rule. Anthropic's improved results are not tied to chip savings and are not shown to last, and the packet has no evidence on OpenAI. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'The result of this bubble bursting will be' is firm, and it depends on the bubble bursting, so the antecedent is kept. There are no thresholds and no deadline.

contract.note: Requiring a broad collapse of the AI boom rather than a regional correction is an ordinary reading of 'this bubble'. Requiring all three consequences, plus a causal link to the collapse, is fair.

evidence.note: CB Insights reports record venture funding through Q3 2026. That does not show a collapse; it bears on the condition only.
J.P. Morgan reports AI taking a concentrated share of venture capital. This shows no collapse of the AI boom.
TechRadar, citing Reuters, reports a selloff in Chinese AI stocks. This is a regional decline, not the broad collapse the antecedent requires.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish the antecedent, a broad bursting of the AI bubble. Funding data through Q3 2026 show record AI investment, and the Chinese selloff is only regional. Because the condition's status is unknown, the forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: The 'would' clauses depend on OpenAI failing to restructure within two years, which triggers the debt conversion. The antecedent is kept correctly.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats completing the restructuring as making the prediction inapplicable, not false.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure, dated 2025-10-28, that its recapitalization is complete, within the two-year window. It shows the antecedent did not occur. It is evidence about the condition, not the outcome, so it cannot contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI completed its recapitalization in October 2025, inside the two-year window. That meets the contract's early-resolution rule. The investment did not convert to debt, so the predicted consequences never had a chance to occur and the conditional is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'You're going to get' is a firm forecast. 'Before then' ties the stories to the predicted pullback in hyperscaler spending, and the proposition keeps that link.

contract.note: Requiring a recurring theme across outlets is a fair reading of 'a lot'. Treating the pullback as setting the order of events is a reasonable reading. Asking for evidence of desperation beyond the topic of the stories is strict, but defensible.

evidence.note: A Scientific American story after the post presents test-time compute as an alternative route to improvement. It partly supports the coverage element, but not the claimed desperation.
A TechCrunch story covers gains from inference-time search, while including skeptical experts. It is a second independent example of the theme.

reviews.rationale: Two independent stories show the theme appeared, but that falls short of 'a lot', and nothing shows desperation. The qualifying hyperscaler pullback has not been verified, so the required order of events is not established, and there is no deadline.
